stem: Under the European Web Accessibility Directive (Directive 2016/2102), what transparency requirement must public sector bodies fulfill on their websites?

options.text: They publish an accessibility statement, an accessible feedback mechanism, and a link to national enforcement procedures.
options.shortLabel: Accessibility statement, feedback, and enforcement link
options.rationale: Article 7 of Directive (EU) 2016/2102 explicitly requires public sector bodies to provide a detailed accessibility statement, an accessible feedback mechanism for reporting barriers, and a direct link to the competent enforcement procedure.

options.text: They publish a detailed conformance report for each website but do not provide a feedback mechanism.
options.rationale: Article 7 requires an accessibility statement, a feedback mechanism, and a link to enforcement; a conformance report alone does not satisfy the transparency requirement.

options.text: They display a WCAG conformance badge issued by a nationally accredited certification body.
options.rationale: The directive permits self-assessment and does not require third-party certification or a WCAG badge.

options.text: They publish an accessibility policy reviewed annually by the national enforcement body, without a statement of non-accessible content.
options.rationale: The accessibility statement must identify non-accessible content and provide feedback and enforcement routes; annual review by the enforcement body is not the prescribed mechanism.

explanation: Directive (EU) 2016/2102 requires public sector bodies across EU member states to ensure their websites and mobile applications conform to accessibility standards (EN 301 549 / WCAG). Under Article 7, organizations must fulfill a specific three-pillar transparency requirement: (1) publish a detailed accessibility statement explaining compliance status and non-accessible content, (2) provide a feedback mechanism allowing users to notify the organization of barriers, and (3) include a link to the enforcement body to which users can escalate unaddressed complaints.
